lead_in: Luke 16:9’s “mammon of iniquity”: Augustine on how not to misread it, and what giving alms from rightful labor means.

excerpt.text: That we may express the whole then in Latin, our Lord Jesus Christ says this, Make to yourselves friends of the riches of iniquity. Some, by a bad understanding of this, plunder the goods of others, and bestow some of that upon the poor, and so think that they do what is enjoined them. . . . Give alms of your righteous labours: give out of that which you possess rightfully.
excerpt.attribution: St Augustine, Sermon 63 on the New Testament (Ben. 113), §2, in Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 6
